aspect: Regression is the standard response and is read as misbehaviour
description: Bedwetting, clinging, loss of acquired speech, return to baby talk. Save the Children found three quarters of Gazan children bedwetting in fear in 2022, with a growing number showing reactive mutism.
energy_note: Punished for going backwards under a bombardment.

aspect: The Second Intifada numbers, for the same picture twenty years earlier
description: Mousa and Madi 2003: 46% of parents reported aggression in their children, 38% worse school results, 27% bedwetting, 39% nightmares.
energy_note: The same four symptoms, every war, every decade.

description: 56% of Gazan 10-12 year olds reported recurrent nightmares, averaging 4.2 nights a week with a mean duration of about 2.5 years. In the Better Learning Programme cohort of 1,093 children, the average was 4.86 nights a week before treatment.
time_note: Mean duration ~2.5 years of recurrent nightmares.
energy_note: Two and a half years of being afraid to go to sleep.

aspect: Attachment disruption, because the parent is not available
description: A terrified or grieving parent cannot provide the regulation an infant needs. The child's stress system is calibrated in that period, and it is calibrated to the parent's state, not the bombs.
energy_note: The war reaches the baby through the mother's face.

description: A systematic review of 83 studies shows children exposed to recurrent or severe trauma are at significant risk of cognitive impairment, social-emotional-behavioural problems and academic difficulty - on top of the days simply not attended.
money_note: Lifetime earnings effect of lost schooling years.
energy_note: The gap widens by itself for the next ten years.

aspect: SECONDARY - the diagnosis arrives in the destination country, wrongly
description: Resettled children present as inattentive, oppositional or delayed and are assessed by systems with no trauma-informed context and often no shared language. Misdiagnosis in both directions is routine.
energy_note: Labelled for life by a fifty-minute assessment.
